title: Indian Climbers Make First Recorded Indian Ascent of Tharang II Peak
excerpt: Subhajit Banerjee and Suresh Singh summited the 6,027-metre Miyar Valley peak on 22 September via a new West Ridge line named Moonlight Spur.
body:
• Subhajit Banerjee and Suresh Singh summited Tharang II (6,027 metres) in Himachal Pradesh's Miyar Valley on 22 September 2026, in what available records suggest is the first recorded Indian ascent.
  • The pair opened a new upper line, the West Ridge route they named Moonlight Spur, after climbing the Centre Spur of the south-west face.
  • The 10-member Transcend Adventures expedition ran from 11 to 22 September, without guides, Sherpas, high-altitude porters or fixed ropes, according to the expedition report.
  • The peak, also called Shailaputri, was first climbed on 1 October 2016 by Charlie French of Britain and Anette Kinde of Sweden.

Indian climbers Subhajit Banerjee and Suresh Singh reached the summit of Tharang II, a 6,027-metre peak in the Miyar Valley of Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh, on 22 September 2026. Available published records suggest it is the first recorded Indian ascent of the peak, according to the expedition report published by Dream Wanderlust and reporting by The Hindu BusinessLine, which described Transcend Adventures as the first Indian team to scale the peak.

Banerjee and Singh reached the summit at 4:30 p.m. after an 18-hour push that began at 5:15 a.m. from Summit Camp and ended with a return to that camp at about 11:30 p.m., the expedition report said.

A new line on the upper mountain

The team climbed the Centre Spur of the south-west face and then followed the west ridge to the summit, Padamati Anvitha of Transcend Adventures told BusinessLine. The expedition report gives more detail: after reaching the top of the spur at about 11:30 a.m., Banerjee and Singh moved onto the West Face, put on crampons, and chose the West Ridge, which they named Moonlight Spur.

That upper section involved about 90 metres of ice at around 70 degrees, followed by mixed climbing and dry-tooling, with heavy cornice formation requiring careful route choice, the report said. The overall difficulty was reported as grade AD. The ascent was completed without guides, Sherpas, high-altitude porters or fixed ropes.

"The team opened a new route. They climbed the Centre Spur of the southwest face and then followed the west ridge till the summit."

— Padamati Anvitha, Transcend Adventures, via The Hindu BusinessLine

The expedition, camp by camp

The 10-member team began its approach from Manali on 11 September and reached Base Camp at Doksa, at 3,700 metres, the same day after trekking from Khanjer, the last roadhead, the expedition report said. Camp 1 was established at 4,260 metres and Camp 2 at 4,900 metres, with Summit Camp below the south-west face at 5,256 metres on 19 September. BusinessLine reported similar camp heights, at approximately 3,700, 4,260, 4,820 and 5,270 metres.

A first summit attempt on 20 September retreated from about 5,958 metres because of loose rock, rockfall risk and lack of time, the report said. The rest of the team then descended to Camp 2, while Banerjee and Singh stayed at Summit Camp for the successful second attempt.

BusinessLine listed the other team members as Rency Thomas G, Mukesh Rana, Padamati Anvitha, Nandigama Rajkumar, Barmavath Mothikumar, Vislavath Bunny, Jayesh Dhirajlal Salla and Mimraj Rana, alongside Banerjee and Singh. The expedition report lists the same team, with Mimraj Rana as cook.

The peak and its climbing history

Tharang II, also known as Shailaputri, is part of the Tharang Massif. Its south-western side is predominantly rocky, while its northern aspect has ice, snow seracs and a complex glacier system, the expedition report said.

Both sources identify the first ascent as 1 October 2016, by British climber Charlie French and Swedish climber Anette Kinde via the south-west face. No earlier Indian ascent was found in the available published records, the expedition report said, which is why the 2026 climb is described as the first recorded Indian ascent rather than a first ascent overall.

Read the full expedition account at Dream Wanderlust and the news report at The Hindu BusinessLine.
